title: Crossing the PAL crossroads: De novo gene birth in plant scent diversification and the pathogenic arms race
content: De novo genes, which play a pivotal role in regulating various metabolic pathways within plants, are newly emerged, lineage-specific genetic sequences that originate from non-coding regions of DNA. The recent role of these genetic architects in scent diversification was reported by Li et al. (2025). This viewpoint explores how this floral fragrance-regulating de novo gene also influences the plant defense system against pathogens. In contrast, pathogens use the de novo gene mechanism to generate virulence factors, creating an evolutionary arms race. Understanding the mechanism of de novo gene birth could open new frontiers for improving plant resistance to pathogensFloral scent results from a complex biochemical network that intersects with the salicylic acid-mediated defense pathway in plants.
